\section{Numerical validation}\label{sec:N6}

% N6-p1
Every numerical statement in this section carries one of four evidence classes - exact algebra evaluated numerically, exact diagonalisation at $n \le 12$, synthetic finite-shot sampling at stated shot budget, and TEBD at $n \le 20$ - and the paper contains no quantum hardware data. Every reconstructed quantity is compared against its independently computable validation reference, the dynamic-programming lattice content dressed by the perturbation series. The campaign answers one question with a stated failure condition: does a coupling window exist in which the reconstruction still agrees with the reference while the dynamics under $V_{\mathrm{XXZ}}$ is entangling, the convergence boundary set by local resonances $|a_i - a_j|$ rather than the global Weyl disc? An empty join would restrict the protocol to sensing mode. These comparisons establish agreement with the classical reference under trusted assumptions, short of certification.

% N6-p2
Under synthetic finite-shot sampling over the benchmark instance set, data source SYN-N12c, decoder coverage is the $K$-independent geometric erasure count: 252 of 264 steps feasible. A step whose dial feasibility window is empty - the pair-gap visibility ceiling below the third-cluster isolation floor - is recorded as an erasure carrying the flagged ratio-1 maximum-likelihood default, excluded from conditional accuracy, and stays erased. Figure~\ref{fig:nf5} scores the feasible steps against the reference: the decoder snaps chained ratio estimates to the small-integer hypothesis class, aggregates by trial median, and should gain accuracy as shot noise falls below the gap scales. Single-trial and trial-median conditional accuracy are reported against shot budget $K$, full-profile recovery against $K$, and the ratio-1 imputation variant as its own clearly separated curve, with 95\% bootstrap intervals throughout. The claim is benchmark-specific - estimation then constrained decoding over a controlled hypothesis class, maximum degeneracy two - and reaches neither readability below the visibility floor, decoding beyond the tested class, nor performance outside the benchmark family.

% N6-p3
The dynamical half of the question is measured by exact diagonalisation at $n \in \{8, 10, 12\}$, data source ED-N11. Under $V_{\mathrm{XXZ}}$ the dynamics is entangling from the perturbative disc edge $J_{\mathrm{disc}} = 1/(4(n-1))$ upward, with required bond dimension $\chi_{\mathrm{req}}$ of 3 to 4 and saturated half-cut entanglement entropy $S_{\mathrm{vN}}$ of 0.5 to 1.3. Both quantities are flat in $n$ - $n = 8$ matches $n = 12$ to two decimals - which is the behaviour of localised cluster resonances rather than volume-law growth. Entangling does not mean computationally hard. The curves are measured per system size on the benchmark instance sequence and drawn as individual curves per size, never as a min-max band, and instance-to-instance bands are deferred.

% N6-p4
The operating model is a random-field XXZ chain - the diagonal disorder $a_i \sim n^{2}$ arises from the instance weights - so the Bethe-ansatz integrability of the clean XXZ chain is broken. The applicable frame is the localisation physics of disordered spin chains, and that frame predicts both a flat-in-$n$ bond-dimension band and deepening localisation as the disorder scale $W \sim n^{2}$ outruns a fixed coupling $J$. Under it the measured flatness is expected physics rather than a small-size artefact. The frame explains the band and generates a testable prediction - it does not by itself establish or exclude hardness at any size.

% N6-p5
Sizes beyond $n = 12$ are inaccessible to exact diagonalisation, so we extend the measurement to $n = 20$ with TEBD in the Vidal gauge, the diagonal fields folded into the bond gates so that the Trotter commutator scales as $J^{2} a$ rather than $J a^{2}$. Validation precedes production: against the exact results at overlapping sizes the maximum entropy deviation is of order $10^{-6}$ to $10^{-7}$, the required bond dimension agrees in 12 of 12 cells, and step-halving checks are flat. The production sweep over $n \in \{14, 16, 20\}$ and $J$ from 0.05 to 0.5 completes 24 of 24 cells with zero bond-dimension cap hits, data source TEBD-N14. Across $n = 8$ to 20 - a 2.5$\times$ span joining exact diagonalisation to TEBD - $\chi_{\mathrm{req}}$ stays in $\{2, 3, 4\}$, flat to falling, and the $S_{\mathrm{vN}}$ saturation is instance-dominated and $n$-independent. The flat-to-falling band is the deepening localisation the disorder frame predicts. Past the exact-diagonalisation wall the TEBD results cover state properties only, caps are reported as cap hits rather than truncated, and the run measures tested instances rather than a scaling law.

% N6-p6
The certificate's operating statement is read per degenerate target rather than globally in $J$: the fingerprint and the decoded profile are co-located on targets of degeneracy $g \ge 2$ by construction, so the join of decoding accuracy and fingerprint response is evaluated target by target. The per-target reading narrows the claim - a window statement quotes the targets on which both members of the join hold, and no global-in-$J$ guarantee is implied.

% N6-p7
The measured join is nonempty. The operating window runs from the perturbative disc edge $1/(4(n-1))$, numerically 0.023 to 0.036 at tested sizes, up to $J \approx 0.1$, with operating point $J^{*} \approx 0.05$. Within it three measurements hold simultaneously. The dynamics is entangling and interacting - $\chi_{\mathrm{req}}$ of 3 to 4, $S_{\mathrm{vN}}$ of 0.5 to 1.3, from exact diagonalisation. The interacting-only tilt fingerprint clears the shot-noise floor under synthetic finite-shot sampling at production $K = 10^{5}$: separation 2.1 to 2.5$\times$ for $J \le 0.05$, 1.5$\times$ at $J = 0.1$, gone by roughly 0.15. The degeneracy profile decodes - 100\% in the unlimited-shot exact read, 82 to 89\% under synthetic finite-shot sampling at total budget $S_{\mathrm{tot}} = 8 \times 10^{5}$. Both window edges are classically computable dial settings - perturbative validity below, fingerprint escape above. The failure condition did not fire - certificate mode operates, and sensing mode is the floor beneath it, not the fallback. The edges are approximate measured values on the benchmark family - the lower varies with $n$ through the disc-edge formula - and the verdict is a measurement at the sizes tested rather than an asymptotic guarantee.

% N6-p8
Figure~\ref{fig:nf6} aligns three panels on the coupling axis $J$. The fingerprint under test is the interacting-only tilt channel, predicted to respond as $J^{2}$ on degenerate targets and escape above the window. Panel (a) shows the fingerprint separation from exact diagonalisation with synthetic finite-shot sampling overlaid, data source ED-N13. Panel (b) shows $S_{\mathrm{vN}}$ and $\chi_{\mathrm{req}}$ from exact diagonalisation at $n \in \{8, 10, 12\}$ as individual curves per system size, data source ED-N11. Panel (c) continues $\chi_{\mathrm{req}}$ to $n = 20$ with TEBD on an explicitly marked instance sequence, data source TEBD-N14, with $\chi_{\mathrm{req}}$ reported at the $10^{-4}$ discarded-weight convention under a per-gate truncation tolerance of $10^{-12}$. The alignment is the point - readability and simulation cost are statements about the same dial. Inside the readable coupling range the fingerprint separates while the cost stays small and roughly $n$-independent, rising outside it. The figure supports the operating-envelope statement for tested distinct-weight instances - proof of principle, not hardness of any kind nor an asymptotic scaling law in $n$.
